object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: UMI collision estimates. A UMI associated with a read from a cell is said to have 'collided' if it appears in two or more reads originating from different molecules. To estimate UMI collision rates, two types of information were used. First, reads in the same cell that originate from different genes must have originated from different molecules, and therefore the sharing of a UMI between two such reads was used as an indicator of a collision. Second, for each gene, the number of distinct UMIs associated within it was measured from the data. Based on the assumption that UMIs were sampled uniformly at random from beads, these data were used to estimate the number of intra-gene collisions (see Supplementary Note). The assumption was verified by examining the distribution of UMI counts across cells; the empirical distribution was near uniform with the exception of a handful of UMIs (Supplementary Note Fig. 2).

Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays
object.description: Barcode-based sequence census assays can label biological features, but barcode design and technical noise complicate quantification. Assay-specific tools can be slow, memory-intensive, and hard to standardize across multimodal, multiplexing, and perturbation assays. kITE uniformly quantifies orthogonal barcode assays with fast, memory-efficient kallisto-bustools processing, while qcbc evaluates barcode-set quality and identifies ambiguity from shared subsequences, homopolymers, and low-diversity designs.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: We have demonstrated a broadly applicable approach to align, error-correct, group, and count sequences from orthogonal barcodes to quantify multimodal data such as cell surface protein abundance, to demultiplex samples, and to perform large-scale perturbation experiments. Our approach is fast, memory efficient, and extensible: orthogonal barcode quantifications can be obtained for numerous assays with variable sequence structure such the recently developed spatial RNA-seq assays (Srivatsan et al. 2021) and massively parallel reporter assays (Gordon et al. 2020). This allows future assay developers to avoid producing, validating, and maintaining software implementing ad hoc solutions. Moreover, some current methods are slow, have high memory requirements, and are specifically tailored for specific assays, which can result in batch effects when performing integrative analysis. Methods such as CITE-seq-Count offer extensibility features for different barcode strategies, but are slow and memory-intensive. The speed and efficiency of our approach enables reproducible single-cell analysis in the cloud with tools such as Google Colab. We anticipate that our framework for quantifying orthogonal barcoding assays will be useful as multimodal assays proliferate (Packer and Trapnell 2018), and that our quality control tool will help assay developers avoid pitfalls in barcode design and help practitioners quality control orthogonal barcode assays. Finally, while our approach is currently engineered to correct mismatch errors, robustness to other types of sequencing errors are possible via other methods that could readily be incorporated in our modular framework (Zorita, Cuscó, and Filion 2015; Booeshaghi et al. 2020; Milo S. Johnson, Sandeep Venkataram, Sergey Kryazhimskiy 2022).

object.label: Cellatlas can use an existing barcode onlist or generate one compatible with the FASTQ barcodes.
Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: These universal principles guided our development of cellatlas for universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data. The cellatlas program requires sequencing reads, genomic references, and a seqspec specification file. From there, cellatlas leverages seqspec functionality to auto generate the kallisto technology string that specifies the 0-index position of the cellular barcodes, molecular barcodes, and genomic features such as cDNA or genomic DNA. It also either points to, or generates, a barcode onlist compatible with the barcodes in the FASTQ files. Thus, cellatlas can be used to process data with a single command: cellatlas build -o out -m rna -s spec.yaml -fb bcs.txt -fa genome.fa -g genome.gtf R1.fastq.gz R2.fastq.gz

object.label: Cellatlas uses seqspec to derive kallisto technology strings and run universal preprocessing with a single command.

object.description: Large language models can extract text effectively but may hallucinate content absent from their source. object.description: Genomic variation can reveal mechanisms of human biology and genetic predisposition to disease. relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Birth timing distinguished IT-Plxnd1 projection patterns: E13.5-born neurons projected broadly ipsilaterally, contralate
object.description: Birth timing distinguished IT-Plxnd1 projection patterns: E13.5-born neurons projected broadly ipsilaterally, contralaterally, and bilaterally to striatum, whereas E17.5-born neurons had minimal heterotypic contralateral and striatal projections.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Cell-type similarity decreased with evolutionary distance, species specializations generally appeared on fine taxonomic
object.description: Cell-type similarity decreased with evolutionary distance, species specializations generally appeared on fine taxonomic branches, and cell-type-specific genes diverged substantially even across homologous types.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Cross-species integration of human, marmoset, and mouse motor cortex identified 45 conserved types, including 24 GABAerg
object.description: Cross-species integration of human, marmoset, and mouse motor cortex identified 45 conserved types, including 24 GABAergic, 13 glutamatergic, and eight non-neuronal types, with both one-to-one and many-to-many alignments and lower resolution than single-species taxonomies.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Discrete and continuous variation coexisted at lower taxonomic levels, with transcriptomic, anatomical, and physiologica
object.description: Discrete and continuous variation coexisted at lower taxonomic levels, with transcriptomic, anatomical, and physiological features varying together with cortical depth, favoring a hierarchy of discrete classes and continua over fully discrete typing.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Driver-defined pyramidal populations had distinct projection patterns: IT-Plxnd1 neurons projected bilaterally to cortex
object.description: Driver-defined pyramidal populations had distinct projection patterns: IT-Plxnd1 neurons projected bilaterally to cortex and striatum, ET-Fezf2 neurons reached multiple subcortical targets and corticospinal tract, and CT-Tle4 neurons projected specifically to thalamic nuclei.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Eleven mouse modalities jointly formed five IT clusters along an L2/3-to-L6 continuum; mouse, human, and marmoset IT typ
object.description: Eleven mouse modalities jointly formed five IT clusters along an L2/3-to-L6 continuum; mouse, human, and marmoset IT types aligned at subclass level but remained ambiguous at cluster level.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.label: Higher-level cortical classes were categorically distinct across modalities and conserved across species, while cluster-
object.description: Higher-level cortical classes were categorically distinct across modalities and conserved across species, while cluster-level boundaries became more ambiguous and modality-dependent.

object.label: Medulla-projecting L5 ET cells occurred mainly in epigenetic cluster 0 but also clusters 2 and 3; transcriptomic L5 ET_1
object.description: Medulla-projecting L5 ET cells occurred mainly in epigenetic cluster 0 but also clusters 2 and 3; transcriptomic L5 ET_1 mapped to those clusters, whereas L5 ET_2-4 mapped to clusters 1, 4, and 5 with almost no medulla projections.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.description: MERFISH identified 95 mouse MOp clusters with near one-to-one subclass correspondence to RNA taxonomies and complex laminar organization, including narrow but continuous depth ranges for many glutamatergic clusters and layer preferences for many GABAergic clusters.

relations.statement: This publication reports this result.

object.description: MOp neurons had 7,245 correlated candidate enhancer-gene pairs linking 6,280 enhancers to 2,490 genes; 76% of candidate enhancers had cluster-specific accessibility, while 24% were broadly accessible and linked to broadly expressed neuronal genes.
